strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear practical importance for T2V generation quality
Elegant and principled approach using Bayesian uncertainty through attention entropy disagreement with clear connection to BALD
Practical efficiency design with Bernoulli-masked approximation and layer-wise truncation reducing inference overhead to 8-13%
Solid mathematical foundation with clear formulations (Proposition 1) and intuitive explanations
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple VBench metrics with thorough ablation studies on ensemble size K, noise pool size M, and acquisition functions
Consistent empirical improvements across CogVideoX models (+0.48 quality on 2B, +0.60 on 3B) with effective qualitative examples
Clear presentation with effective figures explaining methodology
weaknesses: Limited core novelty as the approach is primarily an application of established BALD technique to T2V generation without fundamental methodological innovation

Weak theoretical justification for why attention disagreement should reflect model uncertainty in diffusion models (unlike classification where BALD is grounded), with acknowledged nonlinearity bias dismissed as 'practically sufficient'
Incomplete baseline comparisons missing other noise optimization methods (PYoCo, FrePrior, Reno) mentioned in related work that were dismissed as 'not officially supported' rather than reimplemented
Narrow experimental scope limited to CogVideoX models only; no evaluation on other T2V architectures (Runway, Make-A-Video, Hunyuan, Kling), raising generalization questions

Acknowledged method limitations insufficiently addressed: paper admits method 'does not directly affect generation process' and that low-BANSA seeds can produce high-quality videos, suggesting heuristic rather than principled approach
Lack of human evaluation studies; all results rely on VBench (relatively new model-based metric) without perceptual validation that improvements are meaningful
Missing statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests despite only 100 prompts used for correlation analysis
Hyperparameter selection poorly justified with model/prompt-specific requirements (d*=14 for 2B vs d*=19 for 3B) and arbitrary thresholds (τ=0.7) with unclear generalization to new models
Limited analysis of method failures shown in Figure 7; Section 6 acknowledges seeds with low BANSA scores can still produce good videos but doesn't explain when/why this occurs

strengths: Well-motivated and practical problem addressing an overlooked issue in T2V diffusion models where noise seed selection significantly impacts generation quality
Principled technical approach with BANSA grounded in Bayesian uncertainty theory, including formal Proposition 1 (Zero Condition) with correct proof

Exceptionally comprehensive experimental evaluation across four diverse T2V backbones (AnimateDiff, CogVideoX-2B/5B, Wan2.1, HunyuanVideo) with multiple metrics (VBench quality/semantic, FVMD, user studies)
Thorough ablation studies examining all major design choices (acquisition functions, ensemble sizes, masking probability, layer selection, noise pool size) with proper statistical validation
Insightful analysis experiments revealing mechanistic insights: cross-prompt noise selectivity (Table 1), attention consistency correlation (Table 2), and improved latent dynamics (Table 3)
Practical plug-and-play method requiring no model retraining with reasonable computational overhead (10-15%) and compatibility with existing refinement methods
Rigorous evaluation methodology including blind user study with 12 evaluators and confidence intervals across 10 independent runs
Consistent improvements across all tested models and diverse semantic categories, demonstrating generalizability
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty - applying existing BALD uncertainty quantification to attention maps represents relatively straightforward domain transfer rather than fundamentally new insights
Modest quantitative improvements of only 1-2% on VBench quality scores, raising questions about perceptual significance given 10-15% computational overhead

Insufficient theoretical justification for core assumption that attention disagreement strongly predicts generation quality; alternative mechanisms (model overconfidence vs. genuine quality correlation) not explored
Imperfect empirical correlation between BANSA and quality (Figure 5b shows substantial scatter), suggesting attention uncertainty necessary but insufficient for predicting generation quality
Limited baseline comparisons - primarily against random sampling; missing comparisons with alternative approaches like quality prediction models or deterministic initialization schemes
Methodological heuristics (layer selection via Pearson correlation threshold, global d* across models) lack deep justification; Bernoulli masking approximation accuracy not quantified
Exclusive evaluation on T2V diffusion; transferability to T2I or other modalities unexplored; all experiments use standard inference settings (50-60 steps)
Limited failure analysis and boundary conditions - Figure 6 shows one case but systematic exploration of when/why attention uncertainty fails is absent
Underdeveloped analysis of interesting prompt-dependency phenomenon (Table 1) showing high selectivity; mechanistic understanding of what drives this selectivity missing
Reproducibility gaps including no code availability mentioned, expensive VBench evaluation limiting independent verification, and incomplete implementation details on attention extraction procedures

strengths: Addresses a well-motivated problem with practical significance - noise seed selection significantly affects video generation quality

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple T2V backbones (AnimateDiff, CogVideoX, Wan2.1, HunyuanVideo) with multiple evaluation metrics (VBench, FVMD, user studies) and extensive ablation studies
Practical efficiency: Bernoulli-masked attention sampling and layer truncation enable inference-time deployment with only ~10% computational overhead
Principled theoretical framework grounded in Bayesian uncertainty with Proposition 1 formally establishing the BANSA zero-condition
Rigorous experimental methodology including human evaluation with 12 blind evaluators, statistical validation with 95% confidence intervals, and analysis of failure cases
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty - core contribution is straightforward application of existing BALD-style uncertainty quantification to noise selection, lacking significant innovation

Weak theoretical justification for central claim - paper assumes attention entropy correlates with seed quality but never rigorously establishes why attention disagreement should predict high-quality noise rather than simply uncertain generations
Modest empirical improvements (typically 1-3% on quality metrics) with marginal statistical significance - confidence intervals often overlap between baseline and ANSE methods (Tables 17-19)

Questionable evaluation validity: negative correlations in Figure 5b (r≈-0.67) suggest lower BANSA scores correlate with higher quality, contradicting the claim that BANSA measures desirable uncertainty
Insufficient baseline comparisons - only compares against random sampling and entropy-based selection; lacks comparison to other seed optimization methods or simpler heuristics

Prompt-dependency issues inadequately addressed - Experiment 1 shows same seed fails across prompts but paper lacks systematic analysis of when/why this occurs and whether BANSA accounts for prompt context
Limited scope: purely inference-time seed selection that optimizes within existing model capability rather than improving fundamental model behavior or generation quality
Hyperparameter complexity (p, d*, M, K) with unclear sensitivity analysis and insufficient generalization testing on out-of-distribution prompts

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification: The paper clearly demonstrates that initial noise seed choice significantly affects T2V generation quality, addressing a practical but overlooked aspect of diffusion models
Theoretically grounded approach: BANSA is elegantly formulated using Bayesian uncertainty through attention entropy with formal theoretical justification (Proposition 1)
Highly practical and efficient: Bernoulli-masked approximation enables inference-time deployment without retraining, with only ~10% computational overhead across models

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Extensive evaluation across multiple T2V backbones (AnimateDiff, CogVideoX, Wan2.1, HunyuanVideo), multiple metrics (VBench, FVMD), human studies (12 evaluators), and thorough ablation studies with statistical significance testing

Insightful analytical experiments: Three well-designed experiments convincingly demonstrate that BANSA identifies seeds with prompt-specific improvements, stable attention patterns, and better latent dynamics
Consistent and convincing results: Strong improvements across diverse models and prompts, with visual quality clearly demonstrated in qualitative comparisons
Strong reproducibility: Detailed implementation specifics, clear algorithm descriptions, and promise to release code facilitate reproduction
Excellent presentation of results: Well-structured paper with clear figures, comprehensive tables, and principled statistical validation
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: The fundamental concept of using attention uncertainty for active selection builds heavily on established methods (BALD, uncertainty estimation); the contribution is primarily the application domain rather than methodological innovation

Empirical layer selection procedure: The method for selecting representative layers via correlation analysis is somewhat ad-hoc, with different thresholds for different models (d*=10 vs 14 vs 19), providing unclear guidance for practitioners applying this to new architectures

Attention-level uncertainty limitations: The method operates at attention level which 'does not fully account for semantic or aesthetic quality' as acknowledged; Figure 6 shows failure cases where BANSA still selects seeds producing unnatural content

Concerning reversal experiment: Table 9 shows that selecting seeds with highest BANSA scores degrades quality, suggesting the relationship between attention uncertainty and generation quality may not be straightforward
Limited scope of evaluation: Evaluated only on T2V models with similar architectural families; unclear generalization to image generation, 3D models, or fundamentally different architectures
Noise pool size assumption: The method assumes predefined noise pool (M=10); limited practical guidance on choosing M for new applications, and optimization of this parameter remains unclear
Missing alternative comparisons: No comparison with other recent noise initialization strategies on identical settings, and limited exploration of alternative uncertainty metrics beyond entropy
Incomplete failure analysis: Limited discussion of failure modes and when/why the method breaks down beyond the single example in Figure 6
Design choices lack full justification: Why Bernoulli masking specifically? Why per-layer entropy? Some design decisions appear empirically driven without exhaustive comparison to alternatives
Incremental quantitative improvements: While consistent, the absolute improvements are moderate (~2-4% on VBench metrics), limiting the practical impact in some applications
